Decreased precipitation and increased temperatures result in increased wildfires; which are a bane to these Tree Yuccas."
content.text: Joshua Trees (Yucca brevifolia) are at risk of losing much of their current habitat in Joshua Tree National Park due to climate change (among other ecological and political issues). Decreased precipitation and increased temperatures result in increased wildfires; which are a bane to these Tree Yuccas.Can they also grow from a cutting or when the branches fall and burrow into the sand?Correct !! And the solar industry is still cutting down entire Joshua Tree forests as we speak. Google “Who approved the Aratina Solar Project.”The tree needs to freeze and die to keep going on.. how come that part is not talked about?Funny to see you here as well as El Cerrito, as I spend time in both places. Both amazing habitats. Apparently some Joshua Trees reproduce via rhizomesI stopped at Joshua Tree on the way out of California after Twitchcon. They are incredible! Sad to hear they are in danger. 😢There’s also now 2 Joshua tree species! The original “Western Joshua Tree” (Yucca brevifolia) and the newer “Eastern Joshua Tree” (Yucca jaegeriana). The western species is more “tree” shaped while the eastern species is more “shrub” shaped!A little question, do you know something about the juan fernandez archipelago in chile??? 🇨🇱I'm glowing 3 Joshua trees from seed! They have like 3 leaves. I can give you one! I'm in California ☺️
